checks.title: PATH has no duplicate entries
probe: u=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep . | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
checks.remedy: De-duplicate PATH in your shell rc; usually an rc file sourced twice
checks.notes: Duplicates are rarely fatal but they are a reliable symptom: an rc file sourced twice, or a version manager initialised in both .zshrc and .zprofile. That same double-initialisation is what produces the version-manager conflicts in layer 4, so this is worth surfacing before those checks confuse someone. Reports the count of duplicates rather than listing them, because the paths are machine-identifying.

checks.title: Node resolves to one install
checks.remedy: Remove the shadowing install, or fix PATH order so the intended node wins
checks.notes: Two node binaries on PATH is the classic 'works in my terminal, fails in the script' cause: an interactive shell picks the nvm one, a non-interactive script picks /usr/local/bin. Walks PATH directly because `command -v -a` is a BASHISM -- macOS /bin/sh rejects it with 'invalid option', the error goes to stderr, and `wc -l` then counts zero, reporting 'no installs' for a tool that is plainly installed. That false answer shipped in the first draft of this file and was caught by reading the captured evidence rather than the rendered verdict. sort -u collapses duplicate PATH entries pointing at one binary, so this counts distinct installs. Deliberately NOT isolated: the question is what THIS shell resolves, and clearing the environment would answer a different one.

checks.title: Node is on PATH in a clean environment
checks.probe: command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo found || echo missing
checks.remedy: Install node system-wide, or configure the version manager in a non-interactive-safe rc (.zshenv / .profile)
checks.notes: The .zshrc false negative, checked directly. applies_if runs unisolated by rule (MANIFEST_SCHEMA.md: the gate decides relevance, the probe measures the answer), so this asks: given node exists in your shell, does it still exist without your dotfiles? A no means CI, cron, and any non-interactive script will not find it, while your terminal works perfectly. That rule was written because of this check -- when the gate was isolated too, it failed in the clean environment and the check resolved N/A, silently skipping the exact problem it exists to detect.

checks.title: Shell startup prints nothing to stdout
checks.remedy: Move echo/banner output in your shell rc behind an interactive guard: case $- in *i*) ... esac
checks.notes: An rc file that echoes a banner corrupts every command substitution in every script that starts a login shell -- $(ssh host cat file) silently gains a line. It is a real and under-diagnosed breakage. Measures bytes rather than capturing the text, because the text may contain machine-identifying detail. A generous timeout: a slow rc is itself common and killing it would report the wrong finding.
